fences.rule: Across the passage the same habit is read from the rule's side rather than the load's: there it is an obsolete power still obeyed, here it is told by what removal returns, nothing for a tin and dread for a vessel.
fences.case: The grandmother who lived through the hunger years and keeps a tin of string too short to use.

fences.rule: If money given away converts into respect by how completely the giver lets go, it belongs there; if the gift pre-empts a seizure and moves the load into the obligation of those who received it, it is here.
fences.case: The bankrupt who buys the whole bar a round the week before the bailiff's van.

fences.rule: If what is redescribed is a verdict on one's judgment, whose kind changes from finding to move, it belongs there; if it is an imposed loss redescribed as chosen and kept as a rule that does real work, it is here.
fences.case: The immigrant told his qualifications are worthless who learns that the man saying so employs him at half rate.
